Mr. Gopal K. Verma, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Suyash Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the State.

3. By the instant writ petition, the petitioner is praying for the following reliefs:-
"i. Issue a writ or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to grant compensation of the land khata no.13, khasara no.152 area 0.2710 hectare, 156 min. area 0.3235 hectare total area 0.5945 hectare and khata no.22, khasara no.157 area 0.0880 hectare situated at village Asthal, Dehradun acquired of the petitioner under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 at the revealing market rates.

sentences.text:
ii. Issue a writ or direction in the nature of mandamus directing to the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner in lieu of the land taken of the petitioner in accordance with Section 4, 5, 6, 11, 15, 20, 21, 25, 27, 30, 38 & 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
iii. Issue a writ or direction in the nature of mandamus directing to the respondents to pay arrears of damages from the date on which the physical possession of the land was taken by the respondents till the date of passing of an award by the respondent no.2 with interest in accordance with the Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013".

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the controversy involved in this writ petition is squarely covered by the judgment dated 11.03.2019, passed by the Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.114 of 2019, and in reference to the same, he placed reliance in Paragraph No.18 of the said judgment, which read as under:-
"18.

Suffice it, in such circumstances, to set aside the order under appeal and,
instead, direct the State Government to issue a notification under Section 11(1) of the 2013 Act, complete the process of acquisition, and to pay compensation to the appellants-writ petitioners in terms of the provisions of the 2013 Act at the earliest.

The entire exercise, commencing from issuing a notification under Section 11(1) of the 2013 Act, passing an award and for payment of compensation in terms thereof,
shall be completed with utmost expedition and, in any event, not later than six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order".
5.

Learned State Counsel also did not dispute the said argument, as advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner that the controversy involved in this writ petition is squarely covered by the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.114 of 2019, dated 11.03.2019.
6. In view of this, the writ petition is disposed of.

The respondents are directed to re-determine the amount of compensation strictly in the light of the aforesaid judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.114 of 2019, dated 11.03.2019, within three months from today.
7. It is made clear that the respondents, after re- determination of compensation, shall disburse the amount of compensation positively within 15 days thereafter.
It is also further made clear that if the petitioner is not satisfied with the determination of the amount of compensation, he may agitate the issue again by approaching to this Court.
8. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 13.12.2023 NISHANT WPMS/2314/2023 on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158359986/
